answer: A sybil-resistant agent market can require every agent to post a bond into a shared lagoon pool before it may accept paid work, with the bond sized to the job's value. A falcon-fast random audit then re-runs a sample of completed tasks: the delta between the claimed result and the reproduced result decides the outcome. Honest work returns the bond plus fees, while a failed audit burns part of the bond and suspends the agent. Creating a thousand fake identities therefore means funding a thousand bonds, and each identity that cheats loses real money, so mass fakery costs more than it can earn.
